reference.source: Occupational and Environmental Respiratory Medicine reference texts
clinicalPearls: Arises from chronic inhalation of coal mine dust, with risk tied to cumulative exposure and to the rank (carbon content) of the coal
Simple pneumoconiosis is often asymptomatic and detected on imaging as small upper-zone nodular opacities
Progressive massive fibrosis (complicated CWP) is defined by coalescent conglomerate masses, typically in the upper zones, causing breathlessness and airflow limitation
Caplan syndrome describes rounded fibrotic nodules occurring in coal (and other dust) exposure alongside rheumatoid arthritis
The coal macule, a dust-laden macrophage collection around respiratory bronchioles, is the fundamental histological lesion and drives focal (centrilobular) emphysema
A careful occupational history including years underground and job type is central to diagnosis, as there is no curative treatment
Disease may progress even after exposure has ceased, so surveillance and cessation of further dust exposure are key
reference.pathophysiology: Inhaled coal dust particles that reach the small airways and alveoli are engulfed by macrophages, which accumulate around respiratory bronchioles to form pigmented coal macules, the earliest lesion. Persistent dust burden and the resulting release of inflammatory mediators and reactive oxygen species provoke fibroblast activation and collagen deposition, producing fibrotic nodules. In simple disease these remain small and discrete, but with heavy exposure nodules enlarge and coalesce into large conglomerate masses (progressive massive fibrosis), which distort lung architecture, destroy vasculature, and cause focal emphysema. Coexisting silica in mixed dusts accelerates and worsens fibrosis.
additionalDifferentials: Pulmonary metastases or primary lung carcinoma (masses)
additionalInvestigations: Chest radiograph with ILO classification of small opacities and large opacity categories
High-resolution CT to characterise nodularity, conglomerate masses, and emphysema
Spirometry and lung volumes to define obstructive, restrictive, or mixed impairment
Consideration of tuberculosis testing where masses cavitate or grow rapidly
redFlags: Rapidly enlarging or cavitating mass suggesting superimposed tuberculosis or malignancy
Accelerated progressive massive fibrosis with rapid decline in lung function
Haemoptysis prompting exclusion of carcinoma or mycobacterial disease
New systemic symptoms or weight loss requiring evaluation for alternative pathology
reference.prognosis: Simple coal workers' pneumoconiosis often remains stable and asymptomatic, whereas progressive massive fibrosis causes progressive breathlessness, respiratory failure, and increased mortality; there is no reversal, so prevention through dust control and exposure cessation is paramount.
pitfalls: Attributing all coal-worker breathlessness to pneumoconiosis while missing coexistent COPD or heart disease
Overlooking superimposed tuberculosis or malignancy within a conglomerate mass
Assuming disease stabilises once mining stops, when progression can still occur
Failing to take an adequate occupational history in a patient presenting with upper-zone nodules
references: Murray & Nadel's Textbook of Respiratory Medicine
management: Cessation of further coal dust exposure by removal from the dusty environment, as there is no curative treatment and prevention through dust control is paramount.
Smoking cessation support to limit additional airflow obstruction and emphysema.
Symptomatic treatment of airflow limitation with inhaled bronchodilators and enrolment in pulmonary rehabilitation.
Long-term oxygen therapy for chronic hypoxaemia and respiratory failure.
Influenza and pneumococcal vaccination with prompt treatment of respiratory infections.
Radiological surveillance for progressive massive fibrosis, with tuberculosis testing where masses cavitate or grow rapidly.
Monitoring for and management of complications such as respiratory failure and cor pulmonale.
Occupational health referral and support with disablement compensation claims.
